name: Europa Clipper
first: First mission dedicated to characterising the habitability of an icy moon; largest planetary mission spacecraft ever launched (6065 kg, 100-m² solar arrays)
description: Europa Clipper goes to Jupiter to study Europa — a 3,121-km icy moon believed to harbour a global liquid-water ocean beneath a 15-25 km ice shell, the most accessible potentially-habitable environment in the solar system. Launched 2024-10-14 on a Falcon Heavy at C3 41.7. A Mars gravity assist 2025-03 + Earth gravity assist 2026-12 deliver the trajectory; arrives Jupiter 2030-04-11 for orbit insertion. The orbital tour executes 49 close Europa flybys over four years — passing within 25 km of Europa's surface on the closest passes, designed to map the entire moon while limiting the spacecraft's dose in Jupiter's brutal radiation belts. Instruments: REASON ice-penetrating radar, MASPEX mass spectrometer (samples plume material if any), E-THEMIS thermal imager (finds active geysers), magnetometer + plasma instruments confirm ocean depth from induced magnetic response.

events.label: JUPITER ORBIT INSERTION
events.note: 760 m/s burn. 49 Europa flybys over 4 years follow.
